dies in Berlin at 73
articles.body_raw:
SHUBHAJIT ROY
NEW DELHI, APRIL 27

THE FIRST exiled poet, writer
and columnist of independent
Bangladesh, Daud Haider — who
lived in India for 13 years before
leaving for Germany — died in
Berlin on Saturday, his family
and friends confirmed on
Sunday. He was 73.
A prominent figure in mod-
ern Bengali poetry, Haider was
exiled by the Sheikh Mujibur
Rehman governmentin 1974 af-
ter his poem criticising radical-
ism and bigotry in the country
was published in a Bangla daily.
articles.headline: Daud Haider, exiled Bangladeshi poet, dies in Berlin at 73
articles.text: THE FIRST exiled poet, writer and columnist of independent Bangladesh, Daud Haider - who lived in India for 13 years before leaving for Germany - died in Berlin on Saturday, his family and friends confirmed on Sunday. He was 73. A prominent figure in modern Bengali poetry, Haider was exiled by the Sheikh Mujibur Rehman governmentin 1974 after his poem criticising radicalism and bigotry in the country was published in a Bangla daily.
